user.title: Noxcast
user.description: Weather comes from Open-Meteo (free for non-commercial use, no key). This is the household: battery sensors for learning, house load, grid and the feed-in rule. Add your systems, PV arrays and batteries afterwards.

data.grid_invert: Grid sensor counts export as positive

data_description.soc_sensors: Hours in which one of these batteries is full are left out of learning for every PV array, because output may be curtailed. A battery entered with its system already does this for the PV arrays it can curtail; this setting is only needed for batteries that are not entered.
data_description.soc_full_pct: State of charge from which curtailment is assumed.
data_description.house_load: Optional. Enables the load forecast: power of the whole house (W or kW, measurement).
data_description.day_type_entity: Optional: an entity whose state at noon is the day type, e.g. the Workday binary sensor (a holiday then counts as weekend) or an input_select such as home office / office / holiday. Profiles are learned per state.
data_description.grid_power: Optional. Power at the grid connection (W or kW, measurement), positive = import. Shows measured grid energy in the day view instead of a derived one. A system with Self-consumption and no battery needs it: hours in which the household imported little or nothing at times count as "at least this much" in learning.
data_description.grid_invert: Switch on if the grid sensor is positive while feeding in.
data_description.forecast_days: Days the forecast covers, today included (2 to 7). Further ahead the weather forecast says little about the yield.
data_description.feed_in_mode: What the household may feed into the grid, as the grid operator requires it or you want it. Free: everything. At most a power or a share of the PV peak power: the limit below. Zero export: nothing, ever. Every system follows this rule unless its settings name a deviation.

feed_in_limit.name: Feed-in limit
feed_in_limit.description: Only with a limited feed-in rule.

data.feed_in_limit_pct: At most (% of the PV peak power)

data_description.feed_in_limit_w: What the household may feed in at most, e.g. 800 W.
data_description.feed_in_limit_pct: Share of the installed PV peak power, e.g. 60 %.

user.title: System

basics.title: System

data_description.parent: Empty: a system of its own at the household. Otherwise the system this one is a subsystem of, e.g. a device of an EcoFlow Stream system.

settings.title: Settings of {name}
settings.description:
Everything optional. Settings Noxcast does not compute yet are stored and count in a later version; the Installation tab of the panel shows how far each one counts. A subsystem follows its system's regulation and feed-in; a device that does not follow it is a system of its own.

{concept}

data_description.output_limit_w: What the system delivers at most, e.g. 800 W or the AC power of the inverter. With subsystems: what they deliver together. Without a battery, enter it as the PV power sensors measure it at the limit: sensors of DC power show a few percent more than the AC power. When the measurements show a limit, Noxcast suggests it under Repairs.
data_description.regulation: Full power: delivers everything the PV gives (plain inverter). Self-consumption: follows a smart meter and covers the house load. Fixed power: delivers a set power. Holds for all its subsystems. For a power that changes by a schedule, choose self-consumption, or fixed power with the average.
data_description.charges_from: Own PV: the battery sits before the output (compact device, hybrid inverter). The household: own inverter at the house grid, it charges from surplus of the house.
data_description.balance: Switch on if the batteries of the subsystems even out their state of charge (e.g. EcoFlow Stream). Then they get one battery forecast.

fixed.name: Fixed power
fixed.description: Only with the regulation Fixed power.

deviation.name: Deviation from the feed-in rule
deviation.description: Empty: the system follows the household's feed-in rule (integration page → ⋮ → Reconfigure). Set only what differs: an inverter at full power that cannot hold zero export feeds the rest in anyway; a device that keeps covering only the load when its battery is full never feeds in.

data_description.limit_per_phase: Switch on if the limit holds for each phase on its own (several balcony devices on different phases).
data_description.phase: The phase this subsystem feeds into.

menu.title: {name}
menu.description:
Everything inside {name}. ✎ changes what exists, + adds, − removes. Each form saves when you send it.

{diagram}

menu_option_descriptions.edit: The settings of {name} itself, such as regulation and limits
menu_option_descriptions.remove: The next step names what goes with it and asks before anything is removed
menu_option_descriptions.back: To the system this one belongs to
menu_option_descriptions.finish: Closes the dialog. Everything is saved already

array.title: PV array

data_description.azimuth: Compass direction the modules face: 90° east, 180° south, 270° west.
data_description.peak_power: Sum of module nameplate power. With further orientations: only the modules of this first orientation.
data_description.mounting: How the modules are mounted sets how much they heat up in the sun: free behind (balcony, rack) about 30 K, parallel on a tiled roof about 50 K, integrated into the roof about 60 K.
data_description.system: The system this PV array sits in. Empty: the system whose menu you opened it from.

orientation_2.name: Further orientation 2
orientation_2.description: Only for modules on the same power sensors that face another way (e.g. east and west on one input). Tilt, azimuth and the peak power of these modules; leave empty if not needed.

data_description.peak_power: Sum of module nameplate power of this orientation.
Sum of module nameplate power of this orientation.
Sum of module nameplate power of this orientation.

limits.name: Power limit
limits.description: Only if the modules deliver more than an MPPT input or a micro-inverter lets through, so the power stays flat at a maximum on sunny days.

data_description.sensor_limit_w: The limit of one input or micro-inverter in W, as one of the power sensors above measures it (e.g. 800 for an 800 W micro-inverter; sensors of DC power show a few percent more at the limit). Applies to every sensor of this array. The forecast is capped at it; empty = no limit.

data_description.valid_since: Ignore older history, e.g. after moving or re-orienting the modules.
data_description.temp_coeff: Pmax temperature coefficient from the module datasheet, e.g. -0.26. Recommended. Empty = typical value (-0.35); learned only with the satellite filter.
data_description.heating: Own value instead of the mounting: how much the cells heat above the air at 1000 W/m². Empty = from the mounting.

battery.title: Battery
battery.description:
Battery for the surplus simulation (needs the house load). Its system says where it sits: before the output of a device with PV, or at the house grid with its own inverter.

{diagram}

data_description.system: The system the battery sits in; one battery per system. Empty: the system whose menu you opened it from.

limits.name: Limits
limits.description: Charge and discharge limits. Defaults: 0–100 %, no reserve.

data_description.max_soc_entity: Optional: the current charge limit from the device; it takes precedence over the number.
data_description.min_soc_entity: Optional: the current discharge limit from the device.
data_description.reserve: Percent points above the lower limit where discharging stops in practice, e.g. a feed-in stop rule.

power.name: Power
power.description: Power sensor, efficiency and power limits. All optional.

data_description.battery_power: Optional. Power of the battery (W or kW), positive = charging. The Noxcast card shows it in the power flow.
data_description.battery_power_invert: Switch on if the power sensor is positive while discharging.
data_description.efficiency: Empty = default: 95 % before the output of a device with PV, 90 % at the house grid. Inverter losses are already in the measured values.
data_description.max_charge_w: Empty = no limit. Above it, surplus is fed in although the battery still has room.

remove.title: Remove a part of {name}
remove.description: Choose the part to remove. Nothing is removed before you confirm in the next step.

remove_confirm.title: Remove {name}?
remove_confirm.description: Removed with it: {inside}. Its entities and what Noxcast learned for it are removed too. This cannot be undone.

error.sensor_required: Select at least one power sensor.
error.sensor_missing: The selected sensor does not exist.
error.sensor_unit: Power sensors must report W or kW.

error.date_in_future: The date must not be in the future.
error.orientation_incomplete: A further orientation needs tilt, azimuth and peak power.
error.orientation_duplicate: Two orientations are the same. Enter their modules once with the summed peak power.
error.system_has_subsystems: This system holds subsystems. PV arrays and batteries belong to a system without subsystems.
error.limits_order: Lower limit plus reserve must be below the upper limit.
error.soc_unit: The state of charge must be in %.
error.system_taken: This system already has a battery. A second one is a subsystem of its own.

error.fixed_power_needed: The regulation Fixed power needs a value under Fixed power.

user.title: Consumer
user.description: A device with its own sensor. Its power is taken out of the base load and forecast on its own. Next step: the fields for its timing.

data_description.power_sensor: Power of the device in W or kW, state_class measurement. First choice if there is one: energy counters often count in 0.1 kWh steps, too coarse for single hours. Either this or an energy sensor.
data_description.energy_sensor: Instead of power: energy in Wh or kWh, state_class total or total_increasing. A meter that keeps counting and a counter per program both work; unknown between runs counts as no consumption.
data_description.timing: Fixed: runs regardless of surplus and is part of the load forecast. Flexible: its moment should follow the surplus, so it only counts while it runs.

reconfigure.title: Consumer
reconfigure.description: A device with its own sensor. Its power is taken out of the base load and forecast on its own. Next step: the fields for its timing.

data_description.power_sensor: Power of the device in W or kW, state_class measurement. First choice if there is one: energy counters often count in 0.1 kWh steps, too coarse for single hours. Either this or an energy sensor.
data_description.energy_sensor: Instead of power: energy in Wh or kWh, state_class total or total_increasing. A meter that keeps counting and a counter per program both work; unknown between runs counts as no consumption.
data_description.timing: Fixed: runs regardless of surplus and is part of the load forecast. Flexible: its moment should follow the surplus, so it only counts while it runs.

fixed.title: {name}: fixed
fixed.description: Runs regardless of the surplus and is part of the load forecast.

data_description.kind: Profile: median per hour (like base load). Program: runs with an end, learned start times and runs per day (dishwasher). Session: on, then open-ended (PC, TV). Regulated: follows the outside temperature (heat pump, air conditioning).
data_description.remaining_time: Optional: remaining time of the device. A running program then counts until its end.
data_description.elapsed_time: Optional: time the program has run (s, min, h). With the energy sensor it gives the power of the running program, with either kind of counter.

flexible.title: {name}: flexible
flexible.description: You choose when it runs; Noxcast suggests the window. Empty values are learned from the history.

data_description.run_power: Power of a typical run. Empty = learned from its history.
data_description.run_minutes: Duration of a typical run. Empty = learned from its history.
data_description.start_share: The sensor “start now” turns on when a run started now gets at least this share from surplus and about as much as the best window still to come today. Empty = 70 %.
data_description.remaining_time: Optional: remaining time of the device. A running program then counts until its end.
data_description.elapsed_time: Optional: time the program has run (s, min, h). With the energy sensor it gives the power of the running program, with either kind of counter.

options.percent: At most a share of the PV peak power (%)

options.pv_battery: PV with battery in one device

exclude_period.name: Exclude period from learning
exclude_period.description: Ignore a period in which output was curtailed, e.g. holidays with zero export.

relearn.name: Relearn
relearn.description: Learn efficiency and shading again from history now.

init.title: Weather and learning sources
init.description: Weather models for the forecast and archives used when learning from history. Open-Meteo is the default and needs no key; its free API is for non-commercial use.

data_description.weather_models: Open-Meteo models, averaged hour by hour. Default ICON + ECMWF IFS: in a day-ahead test over ten months their mean beat every single model. With several models each one is also archived on its own, so the accuracy panel can compare them. "Compare weather models" in the accuracy panel shows which models suit your installation.
data_description.archive_temperature: Needed to learn the temperature loss. Without it, efficiency absorbs the average temperature.
data_description.satellite: Uses satellite irradiance to select clear hours for learning. Optional; quality varies by region.
data_description.api_key: Only for commercial or self-hosted access.

error.archive_failed: The archive could not be reached or returned an error.
error.models_required: Select at least one weather model.
error.model_unknown: Open-Meteo returned no data for these models.
error.model_partial: Open-Meteo returned no data for at least one of these models.

no_arrays.title: Noxcast has no PV array yet
no_arrays.description: Noxcast forecasts nothing until it knows at least one PV array. Add one under Settings → Devices & services → Noxcast → ⋮ → *Add system* and in the system's menu *Add PV array*: the modules measured together (usually one MPPT input) with their power sensor, tilt, azimuth and peak power. Noxcast then learns it from the history right away.

missing_sensors.title: Noxcast is missing sensors
missing_sensors.description:
These entities are configured in Noxcast but do not exist: {sensors}.

They were probably renamed or removed. Select the new entities in the PV array, consumer or battery that uses them (Settings → Devices & services → Noxcast).

weather_unavailable.title: Noxcast gets no weather forecast
weather_unavailable.description: Open-Meteo could not be reached for more than a day, so Noxcast cannot update its forecast. Check the internet connection of Home Assistant. If you changed the weather models in the options, one of them may no longer be offered. The forecast sensors become unavailable a few hours after the last update.

array_check.title: PV array {name}: configuration does not fit the measurements
array_check.description: The measurements of **{name}** do not fit its configuration: peak power, tilt, azimuth or the power sensor may be wrong. In the Noxcast panel under *Learned*, the array shows what to check. Learned shade and efficiency stay questionable until it fits. After a correction, this report goes away with the next learning run (at night, or *Learn again now* in the panel).

limit_suggestion.title: PV array {name}: power seems to be limited at {peak} W

init.title: Power limit for {name}?
init.description:
No sensor of {sensors} delivered more than {peak} W in the last {window_days} days, and they stayed flat at or near that level on {flat_days} days while the sun would have changed it. This looks like a limit of the inverter or of its input.

Set a limit of {limit} W per sensor? The forecast of **{name}** is then capped at it. Until you answer, nothing changes.

other_value.title: Power limit for {name}
other_value.description: The most one sensor of **{name}** delivers, in W as the power sensors measure it ({sensors}). The measurements stayed at {peak} W.

data_description.limit_w: Applies to every sensor of this array. You can change or remove it later in the array's settings under *Power limit*.

abort.limit_gone: The suggestion no longer holds: the array has a limit already, or its measurements no longer show one.

system_limit_suggestion.title: System {name}: output seems to be limited at {peak} W

init.title: Output limit for {name}?
init.description:
Together, the PV arrays of **{name}** ({arrays}) delivered no more than {peak} W in the last {window_days} days, and on {flat_days} days their sum stayed flat at or near that level while the clear sky would have changed it and offered more. This looks like the output limit of the inverter.

Set an output limit of {limit} W for **{name}**? The forecast of its PV arrays together is then capped at it. The value is what the power sensors measure at the limit: sensors of DC power show a few percent more than the inverter's AC rating. Until you answer, nothing changes.

other_value.title: Output limit for {name}
other_value.description: The most the PV arrays of **{name}** ({arrays}) deliver together, in W as their power sensors measure it. The measurements stayed at {peak} W.

data_description.limit_w: What the system delivers at most. You can change or remove it later in the system's settings under *Output limit*.

abort.limit_gone: The suggestion no longer holds: the system has an output limit already, or its measurements no longer show one.

battery_without_pv.title: Which PV arrays charge the battery {name}?
battery_without_pv.description:
The battery **{name}** sits before the output of a device with PV (system **{system}**), but no PV array belongs to that system, so Noxcast cannot tell which arrays charge it. After the update this happens to a battery whose former settings did not name its PV array.

Open the PV arrays behind this device under Settings → Devices & services → Noxcast and choose the system **{system}**. If the battery has its own inverter at the house grid instead, change the system to the template *Battery at the house grid*. Until then Noxcast computes as before.
